title: Dragon Flight
prompt:
Character bible:
Children (draw these the same way on every page):
- Elliott, age 4–5, short straight light-brown hair; big gray-blue eyes; round cheeks; friendly adventurous expression, wearing medieval tunic with belt and boots or casual explorer outfit
- Colette, age 2–3, wavy brown hair in a top knot; large gray-blue eyes; soft cheeks, wearing whimsical princess-meets-adventurer dress with floral or heart motifs
Pets (draw these the same way on every page):
- Winnie, a Chihuahua–Pug mix, tan fur; upright ears; curled tail; small size
Keep these characters consistent. They represent specific real children. Do NOT replace them with generic children or idealized animated characters. Preserve their recognizable facial structure.

GLOBAL SAFETY (IMPORTANT):
- No object intersections or impossible overlaps.
- Clean occlusion: if objects overlap, the front object clearly covers the back object.
- No extra limbs, no duplicated faces, no merged hands/feet.
- Keep dragons anatomically clean: one head, two wings (if winged), four limbs, one tail.
- Keep shapes simple and readable for coloring.

Black-and-white line art coloring page with a strong diagonal flight composition featuring one large flame dragon flying from lower-left to upper-right across the page. Elliott and Colette ride together on the majestic flame dragon, leaning slightly with the motion of flight; their hair and clothing stream gently backward in the wind. The flame dragon appears powerful and noble with wings fully extended and head forward in confident motion. Below, Winnie runs along a winding path beside a river, looking up toward the flying dragon. The valley below includes simple rolling hills, a winding river, and distant mountains. The sky is open and spacious, avoiding crowding the dragon. Medium-close shot with full-page composition filling 75–90% of the page height, clean, printable outlines with medium consistent line weight, clear foreground, midground, and background separation using outlines only, classic children’s storybook illustration style preserving the children's facial structures and proportions exactly, no shading, no color, no gradients, no cross-hatching, no filled black areas, balanced head-to-body proportions, expressive but restrained facial expressions, whimsical warm tone without exaggeration.

Use the attached character sheet reference images as the canonical identity and style.
